summary.title: TP-Link Tapo C211 - IoT Camera Threat Model
summary.description:
Threat model of the TP-Link Tapo C211 pan/tilt indoor Wi-Fi home security camera and its ecosystem, produced for the CMP308 IoT camera investigation (EH3). The model covers the camera device and its firmware, the on-device RTSP/ONVIF services, the Tapo mobile app, TP-Link cloud services (Tapo Care), local network communication, microSD local storage and firmware updates.

Unit under test: base-labelled Tapo C211, but all regulatory identifiers (FCC ID 2BCGWC200V5, IC 31152-C200V5, HVIN Tapo C200V5, KC ref TapoC210) indicate the underlying hardware is the C200 V5 platform, shared across the C200/C210/C211 line. This is relevant to threat applicability: vulnerabilities affecting the C200 hardware and firmware lineage (e.g. CVE-2025-8065 ONVIF SOAP RCE, CVE-2025-14300 unauthenticated connectAP, CVE-2025-14299 Content-Length validation) may apply to this device and are to be verified against its actual firmware version.

Connectivity: 2.4 GHz 802.11 b/g/n only (no Ethernet, no 5 GHz); WPA/WPA2-PSK; TLS/AES in transit; supports RTSP and ONVIF.

Scope: hardware teardown and local/network penetration testing are in scope. TP-Link cloud services and Tapo accounts must not be attacked; the unit must not be physically destroyed. Cloud-side components are modelled for completeness but marked out of scope for testing.
